entities.summary:
Bahram II (b. 250 CE) was an economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in Global, known for his contributions to monarchs & rulers.

As the ruler of the Sassanian Empire from 293 CE, Bahram II played a significant role in shaping the empire's economic and political landscape.

His reign was marked by a series of significant events, including the Sassanian-Persian Wars with the Roman Empire and the expansion of the empire's borders through strategic alliances and military campaigns.

Bahram II's legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing the development of economics and social science in the centuries that followed.

The impact of his policies and decisions can still be felt today, with the legacy of the Sassanian Empire continuing to shape the cultural and economic heritage of the Middle East and beyond.

As the last king of the Sassanian Empire, Bahram II's story serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring power of human ingenuity and perseverance in the face of adversity.
